content.title: 26 Great Worship Songs About the Resurrection Beyond Easter Sunday
content.text: The resurrection of Jesus Christ isn’t just an Easter story. It’s the foundation of our faith and our daily hope. Whether you’re planning worship for Easter Sunday, New Year’s services about new life, baptism celebrations, or your regular Sunday worship, you need great worship songs about the resurrection in your setlist. These praise and worship gospel songs about resurrection work year-round. Incorporating some of these ideas in your worship sets will help you lead your congregation to proclaim Christ’s victory over death every single Sunday. Why Resurrection Songs Matter All Year Most worship leaders only think about resurrection songs during Easter. But the power of Christ’s resurrection deserves celebration every week. The empty tomb isn’t a once-a-year truth. It’s the daily reality that changes how we live and worship. Worship songs about the resurrection work great for New Year services when you’re talking about new beginnings. They’re perfect for baptism services that highlight the theme of dying to sin and being raised to walk in newness of life. They fit naturally when preaching about victory, hope, or change. And they give your congregation words to express the life-changing power of the resurrection. Great praise and worship songs about resurrection do several things well. They tell the truth about what Christ did. They celebrate victory over sin and death. They connect what happened then to what happens now in our lives. And they’re accessible for everyone to sing. The empty tomb isn’t a once-a-year truth. It’s the daily reality that changes how we live and worship. Classic Hymns That Still Work Today Don’t skip the old hymns when you’re looking for worship songs about the resurrection. These songs have lasted because they capture deep truth in ways people remember. Because He Lives Bill and Gloria Gaither wrote this modern hymn that connects Christ’s resurrection to daily hope in real ways. The line “because He lives, I can face tomorrow” makes this perfect for New Year services, hard times, or any time your congregation needs hope. Crown Him with Many Crowns This hymn powerfully declares Christ’s victory and reign. You could even create a mash-up with a modern worship song like “Crowns Down” by Josh Baldwin and Gateway Worship (see below). Christ the Lord Is Risen Today Charles Wesley’s hymn remains one of the most known resurrection songs. Don’t save it just for Easter. The “Alleluia” part and the strong melody make it work any time you want to celebrate Christ’s victory. Here’s another version at a little slower BPM: Thine Be the Glory This hymn mixes victory language with a melody everyone can sing. Perfect for communion or response times when you’re pointing to resurrection hope. In Christ Alone Keith Getty and Stuart Townend created this modern hymn that walks through the gospel story with special focus on resurrection power. It’s rich in truth and loved by congregations everywhere. The modern worship anthems below gave given us some great options for declaring resurrection truth all year. Many of these newer songs are becoming “modern classics” that mix deep theology with melodies people can actually sing. Living Hope by Phil Wickham This has become one of the most loved worship songs about the resurrection today. The verses tell the gospel story while the chorus allows the congregation to give praise to God for Christ’s victory over sin and death. Graves Into Gardens by Elevation Worship This powerful song works far beyond Easter Sunday. The picture of going from death to life fits New Year themes, baptism services, or any time you’re preaching about God’s power to change lives. King of Kings by Hillsong Worship This modern anthem declares Christ’s victory and rule, and is also Trinitarian in nature. The line “for the love of Jesus Christ who has resurrected me” makes the resurrection personal. Resurrection Power by Chris Tomlin Written specifically about the power of Christ’s resurrection, this song brings fresh perspective to timeless truth. It highlights the truth of Romans 8:10-11 and reminds us that if Christ lives in us, we have the same power living inside of us that raised Christ from the dead. Forever (We Sing Hallelujah) by Kari Jobe This song beautifully tells the story of the victory that has been won over sin and death because of the reality of the resurrection of Jesus. The inviting line “we sing hallelujah” prompts everyone to naturally join in together. Death Was Arrested by North Point Worship The picture of death being beaten and chains being broken makes this a powerful resurrection song that works well with personal testimony as well. This one works beautifully for baptism services or worship sets about freedom. Christ Is Risen by Matt Maher The bridge of this song is a great proclamation of 1 Corinthians 15:55-57 that works well beyond just Easter Sunday. What a Beautiful Name by Hillsong Worship This song works extremely well to highlight the truths of Philippians 2:6-11. The bridge about death losing its power always hits hard and works year-round. See a Victory by Elevation Worship This song’s declaration of Christ’s victory over the grave makes it very applicable when looking for praise and worship songs about resurrection. The song gives us hope amidst trying circumstances, as it reminds us that the battle belongs to the Lord who has already won the final victory. High-Energy Openers About The Resurrection These upbeat gospel songs about resurrection will invite your congregation to engage from the first note. They work for Easter, New Year, or regular Sunday worship. Alive by Hillsong Young & Free This declaration of life-giving resurrection power works perfectly to open services year-round. Great for youth services or modern worship settings. O Praise the Name (Anastasis) by Hillsong Worship The Greek word “Anastasis” means resurrection, and this song builds from quiet verses to a loud chorus. Great for adding dynamic to your worship set. Good Grace by Hillsong United This joyful celebration of grace includes strong resurrection pictures. This song can serve as a call-to-worship song inviting your congregation to engage together right away. This Is Amazing Grace by Phil Wickham This upbeat opener celebrates the amazing grace of our God, and invites us to lift our eyes to just how worthy Jesus, the Lamb who was slain, truly is. Who You Say I Am by Hillsong Worship The identity change that resurrection brings takes center stage in this modern favorite. Works perfectly for New Year themes of new starts or baptism services. Happy Day by Tim Hughes This upbeat celebration makes resurrection joy impossible to ignore. 6 More Worship Songs About the Resurrection to Consider Below are just a few more options to consider. I Will Rise by Chris Tomlin Resurrection Day by Rend Collective Come Out of that Grave (Resurrection Power) by Bethel Music I Know a Name by Elevation Worship Christus Victor (Amen) by Keith and Kristyn Getty Resurrection Blood by Cody Carnes Using Resurrection Songs for New Year Services New Year services give you a great chance to use worship songs about the resurrection beyond Easter. The themes of new starts, fresh beginnings, and changed lives connect naturally to resurrection power. Think about opening your New Year service with “Alive” or “Graves Into Gardens” to quickly set up the theme of new life. Follow with “Because He Lives” to connect resurrection hope to facing the future with confidence. Close with “King of Kings” or “Living Hope” to declare that the same power that raised Jesus is available for the year ahead. The pictures of change in songs like “Death Was Arrested” and “Graves Into Gardens” work beautifully when paired with New Year messages about leaving the past behind and taking hold of new life in Christ. These praise and worship songs about resurrection help congregations understand that spiritual renewal isn’t just a nice idea. It’s the reality of resurrection power at work. If you need help building better sets be sure to check out this free resource. Using Resurrection Songs in Baptism Services Baptism shows dying to sin and rising to new life in Christ. This makes worship songs about the resurrection perfect for these celebrations. The pictures connect powerfully with the physical act of going under the water and coming back up. “Graves Into Gardens” works really well during or right after baptisms. The themes of change if many of the songs above captures exactly what baptism means. Think about featuring one or two strong gospel songs about resurrection during baptism services. This helps everyone celebrate and understand the meaning of what they’re seeing. For additional baptism songs be sure to check out this blog post. Tips for Using Resurrection Songs Year-Round Remember, you don’t have to save these powerful worship songs about the resurrection for just one or two services per year. Here’s how to use them well throughout your worship calendar: Match songs to sermon themes – When your pastor preaches on victory, hope, change, new life, be sure to pull from your collection of resurrection songs. Songs like “Living Hope” or “See a Victory” support these messages powerfully. Use them during communion – The Lord’s Supper declares both Christ’s death and His resurrection. So worship songs about resurrection naturally fit with communion all year. Add them to regular rotation – Don’t wait for special times. Songs like “What a Beautiful Name” and “In Christ Alone” are strong enough to carry regular Sunday worship while keeping resurrection truth central. Build and release tension – Even outside Easter season, move energy up and down in your sets. Go from celebration to quiet thinking and back to celebration using a mix of upbeat and thoughtful resurrection songs. Connect to real life – When your congregation faces hard times, remind them of resurrection hope through songs like “Because He Lives” or “I Will Rise.” The promise that death couldn’t hold Jesus becomes the promise that nothing can beat those who trust in Him. Scripture to Use with Resurrection Worship Read Scripture in your worship sets during interludes or song intros. Use these key passages as transitions or spoken parts in any service that includes some of the worship songs about resurrection we’ve mentioned in this article. Romans 6:4 – “We were buried with him through baptism into death so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may live a new life.” 1 Peter 1:3 – “Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! In his great mercy he has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.” Ephesians 2:4-5 – “But because of his great love for us, God, who is rich in mercy, made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in sins. It is by grace you have been saved.” 2 Corinthians 5:17 – “If anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come. The old has gone, the new is here!” These passages work beautifully with resurrection songs no matter the season or service type. Building Great Sets with Resurrection Songs Here are a few last practical tips for adding these worship songs about the resurrection into your regular worship planning: Start with purpose – Before picking songs, ask what you want your congregation to understand or feel. Are you celebrating victory? Giving hope? Calling for change? Let your purpose guide your song choices. Mix energy levels – Combine upbeat songs about resurrection with quieter more reflective moments. This creates natural rhythm and helps take people on a journey throughout your worship set . Think about your context – A New Year service might lean more on change and new beginning themes. A regular Sunday might focus more on daily hope. Baptism services talk about identity and freedom. Let the situation guide your song selections. Make it singable – The best worship songs about the resurrection are ones your congregation can actually sing. Focus on melodies people remember and words that are clear over being too complex. We’ve tried to suggest songs that fit this criteria throughout this article. If you need help evaluating strong songs for your master song list, be sure to check out this resource. Final Thoughts The resurrection of Jesus Christ changed everything. It’s not a once-a-year celebration. It’s the daily reality that gives us hope, changes who we are, gives us power for ministry, and promises us eternal life. When you pick worship songs about the resurrection for your services—whether for Easter, New Year, baptism celebrations, or regular Sunday worship—you’re giving your congregation powerful tools to declare life-changing truth. Take time with your song choices. Think about how these gospel songs about resurrection connect to your specific service themes and your people’s needs. Build sets that move people from where they are to where God wants them to be. And remember that the power isn’t in the songs themselves. The power is in the risen Savior those songs declare. … remember that the power isn’t in the songs themselves. The power is in the risen Savior those songs declare. The empty tomb isn’t just history. It’s the hope we need today and every day. Let your worship sets show that world-changing, life-changing reality all year long. Join The Academy! Planning worship services—especially significant ones centered around resurrection themes —requires wisdom, creativity, and ongoing support. If you’re looking for a community of worship leaders who understand exactly what you’re facing, along with practical training and done-for-you resources, I’d love to invite you to check out the Worship Ministry Training Academy. We’ve created a space where worship leaders can learn, grow, and thrive together through every season of ministry. What are your favorite praise and worship songs about resurrection? How do you use resurrection themes beyond Easter Sunday? Share your ideas in the comments below. Help other worship leaders celebrate Christ’s victory year-round! FAQs (Frequently Asked Questions) Why are resurrection worship songs important beyond Easter Sunday? Resurrection worship songs matter all year because the resurrection of Jesus Christ isn’t just an Easter story; it represents victory, new life, and hope that believers celebrate daily. What are some classic hymns about the resurrection that still resonate today? Classic hymns like ‘Because He Lives’ by Bill and Gloria Gaither, ‘Crown Him with Many Crowns,’ ‘Christ the Lord Is Risen Today’ by Charles Wesley, and ‘Thine Be the Glory’ continue to powerfully declare Christ’s victory and reign in worship today. Can you recommend modern congregational worship songs about the resurrection? Yes! Modern worship anthems such as ‘Living Hope’ by Phil Wickham, ‘Graves Into Gardens’ by Elevation Worship, ‘King of Kings’ by Hillsong Worship, and ‘Resurrection Power’ by Chris Tomlin are great examples that highlight the power and victory of Christ’s resurrection. How can resurrection songs be used in services other than Easter? Resurrection songs can be effectively used in New Year services to inspire new beginnings, baptism services to symbolize dying to sin and rising to new life in Christ, and throughout the year to remind congregations of Jesus’ transformative power. What tips are there for incorporating resurrection worship songs year-round? You don’t have to save powerful resurrection worship songs only for Easter; integrating them into regular worship sets, using scripture readings during interludes or songs, and building thematic sets around resurrection help keep the message alive all year long. What is a good approach to building worship sets with resurrection songs? When building great worship sets with resurrection songs, consider mixing classic hymns with modern anthems for variety, include scripture readings to deepen understanding, and select high-energy openers alongside reflective pieces to engage the congregation effectively.
